newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Air China cuts ex-Hong Kong/London rate.
newsitem.headline: Air China cuts ex-Hong Kong/London rate.

text.p: Hong Kong May 1 - Air China is offering cut price cargo rates to try and win market share on its new Hong Kong to London service, industry sources have told Reuters.

Earlier this month and three months before Hong Kong is handed back to Beijing, China's flag carrier began a once weekly flight from Beijing to London Heathrow via Hong Kong . It means extra competition for established carriers, Cathay Pacific Airways Limited, British Airways and Virgin Atlantic.

Industry observers said just one flight per week will initially have a minimal impact on market share currently enjoyed by existing carriers. But they said they are watching with interest to see if, as expected, Air China is granted more frequencies, probably after the handover and when Hong Kong's new airport opens, when it could start to make sizeable inroads.

Cargo marketing sources said that Air China has started selling cargo space for around HK$3 lower than its three rivals. They said the ruling airline market rate from Hong Kong to London Heathrow is around HK$22. Air China is reported to be offering space at HK$18-19. Air China is also reported to be selling passenger tickets for more than HK$1,000 cheaper than the current HK$5,800 advertised economy fare of other carriers.
A BA source said the Hong Kong to London cargo market is currently strong "so there's enough for everyone."
On rate undercutting "if you have a new entrant, one of the ways to build up market share is to offer competitive rates," the BA source said.
Albert Fok, spokesman for Air China's ground handling agents in Hong Kong, Jardine Airport Services Limited, said passenger and cargo demand has been good so far.

Air China has a larger cargo carrying capacity to London than ex-UK because it is using a 747-400 Combi with around 40 tonnes cargo capacity which makes its return flight to Beijing, Fok said. The Combi is operated in rotation with a 747-400 all-passenger plane that flies to London from Beijing and is scheduled to operate the return London to Beijing via Hong Kong route.
If the passenger flight is full from London, Fok said the belly cargo capacity to Hong Kong is around 10- 12 tonnes. - Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+5017
